title: Maple-Walnut Brown Butter
description: Toasted milk solids, smooth walnut paste and a little maple make a finishing butter for squash gravy or soft sweet potatoes.
equipment: 16-cavity tablespoon portion tray or kitchen scale

ingredients.name: smooth unsalted walnut paste
ingredients.note: Pure ground walnuts with no pieces. Stir before measuring.

steps.title: Divide the butter
steps.text: Set aside one quarter of {butter} for browning. Soften the remaining butter just until pliable, about 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Brown the small portion
steps.text: Melt the reserved quarter in the HexClad over medium-low heat for 3–5 minutes, swirling until the milk solids go golden and smell nutty.

steps.title: Cool the brown butter
steps.text: Scrape the butter and browned milk solids into the shallow bowl. Cool for about 15–20 minutes until the mixture is soft and opaque at the edges.

steps.title: Make the walnut base
steps.text: Stir {walnut} and {maple} into the softened butter with a spatula until smooth.

steps.title: Fold and portion
steps.text: Fold in the cooled brown butter and all its browned bits. Divide into sixteen equal portions by weight, about a tablespoon each. Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Melt a portion into hot thickened squash gravy, or fold it through soft sweet potato mash loosened with gravy.

notes: Yield: About 1 cup. One serving is 1 tablespoon, or one sixteenth of the batch. Make ahead: Brown the small portion of butter ahead and refrigerate it. Bring it back to a spreadable texture before folding it in. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions for up to 2 months. The smooth walnut paste keeps its texture after thawing. Fridge reheat: Whisk a cold portion into hot, already thickened gravy off heat until melted. For a leftover meal, first reheat the food and gravy to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw a portion covered in the refrigerator overnight and finish the hot gravy as above. For a dairy-free version, use unsalted plant-based butter and blend it softened with the walnut paste and maple. Omit the browning step for plant-based butter. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/16 of recipe): 103 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 0.6 g total carbohydrate, 11.4 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 1 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
